args.body: the aerodynamic verdict now comes out of the FULL pipeline rather than a check called by hand: 70.0 cm2 against the 34.2 cm2 needed, with C_Lmax 1.48 taken by clade and labelled borrowed. Same number as generation 2 reached directly, by a different route, which is the point: the layers agree because they share one coefficient policy.

detail.launch_airspeed_from: supplied in STATE (assumed: DECLARED by the design, not measured: DESIGN INPUT: sqrt(2gh) for the h = 4 m launch height Bishop 2006 used for Glaucomys volans, ignoring drag, so an upper bound on what a drop can give. Not a measured airspeed of anything.)
detail.C_Lmax_note: C_Lmax 1.48 is BORROWED: it was measured on live Petaurus breviceps (sugar glider, a marsupial) in free glides, mean angle of attack 44.15 +/- 3.12 deg and is applied here to Mus musculus because the NCBI taxonomy places both inside Theria <mammals>. Measured in a marsupial glider and offered across Theria, which is marsupials and placentals together. For any taxon other than Petaurus breviceps this is a BORROW across a clade, and the check labels it so. It is the closest measurement in this repository to a gliding mammal; it is not a measurement of the animal being designed. Taxon Mus musculus, from stated on the design.
detail.C_Lmax_caveat: THIS IS A STALLED-MEMBRANE GLIDE COEFFICIENT, NOT A STEADY-FLIGHT MAXIMUM, and the source is explicit that it was not enough. In the same glides the animals accelerated downward at 1.0 +/- 0.5 m/s2 and forward at 2.1 +/- 0.6 m/s2: Bishop states that body weight was NOT fully supported by aerodynamic force and that some of the lift went into forward acceleration. The angles of attack are far above where an engineered wing stalls. Bishop KL 2006 (J Exp Biol 209:689-701, doi 10.1242/jeb.02062) reports the same for Glaucomys volans, gliding at 35.4-53.5 deg with the wings stalled and accelerating downward, and finds flying squirrels reach higher lift coefficients than sugar gliders -- so 1.48 is, if anything, generous for a mammal without a flying squirrel's specialisations.
detail.C_Lmax_source: Bishop KL 2007, Aerodynamic force generation, performance and control of body orientation during gliding in sugar gliders (Petaurus breviceps), J Exp Biol 210:2593-2606
detail.area_convention: STATE lifting_area_m2 is pectoral + pelvic + caudal (mesh); the coefficient is referred to the whole outstretched body-and-membrane planform, as digitised from the gliding animal. The conventions differ and this check does not correct for it.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
